title: Cloud Connector metrics logs: VM, instance and resource samples

prose.text: Metrics logs are the streamed resource-usage samples of each connector. This subject covers their kinds, timing and missing values.

prose.label: Use.
prose.text: {{siem-thresholds}} The state changes that accompany resource trouble are in [[cloud-connector.logs.event-records]].

checks.do: Whether a gap in instance metrics shows nodata set to True, which points at the connector instance service rather than at the feed.
Whether a zero metric on a resource line is a real value or a metric that does not apply to that resource type.

three-types.statement: Each Cloud or Branch Connector generates three types of Metrics logs: VM (applicable to the whole VM), Instance (per data-processing instance) and Resource (per physical or logical resource that all data-processing instances use).

quotes: There are three types of Metrics logs that each Zscaler Cloud Connector or Branch Connector generates:
VM: Metrics that are applicable at the virtual machine (VM) level.
Instance: Metrics that are applicable at the level of an individual data-processing instance.
Resource: Metrics that are applicable at an individual resource level.
There are physical and logical resources in a Cloud Connector or Branch Connector that all data-processing instances use.

one-minute.statement: All three are collected at one-minute intervals, with one log line per minute for each connector, each data-processing instance and each resource respectively.

quotes: There is one log line per minute for each Cloud Connector or Branch Connector.
There is one log line per minute for each data-processing instance.
There is one log line per minute for each resource.

instances-per-connector.statement: Each Cloud or Branch Connector has between one and three data-processing instances, depending on the form factor.

quotes: Each Cloud Connector or Branch Connector has between one and three data-processing instances, depending on the form factor.

nodata.statement: Instance metrics carry a `nodata` field set to True when no data is available, which indicates an issue on the connector instance service in which the metrics samples were not collected.

quotes: There is also a %s{nodata} field, which is set to True when no data is available. This value indicates an issue on the connector instance service in which the metrics samples were not collected.

not-applicable.statement: On a resource line, metrics that do not apply to that resource type are set to zero or absent.

quotes: Metrics that are not applicable to that resource are set to zero or absent from the log line.

siem-thresholds.statement: The vendor's stated use of VM metrics is SIEM-side alerts when CPU or memory utilization crosses a defined threshold, and of resource metrics is monitoring and notification on disk partition usage.

quotes: you can configure alerts on the SIEM side to monitor the CPU or memory utilization when they cross a defined threshold.
You can set up your SIEM to monitor the usage of disk partitions and send notifications when necessary.
